details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:352 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The jq filter counts `cancelled` cycle runs against the `PROMOTE_CYCLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` retry budget.
  WHY: A cancelled smoke gate is documented as a skip that never counts, but the filter prematurely exhausts the budget and can hold the tip after cancellations; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputes this as intentional for externally cancelled cycle jobs and classifies the issue as documentation-only.

- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:352 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The jq filter omits `startup_failure` from the failed-attempt retry-budget count.
  WHY: A `startup_failure` cycle run never spends the budget, so the same broken tip can be re-dispatched every daily tick; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputes this as intentional because startup failures are deploy-time issues rather than retry-budget attempts.

- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:352; scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:188 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The two schedulers count different conclusion sets against their retry budgets.
  WHY: `auto_release_stable.sh` counts `failure | timed_out | startup_failure`, while `promote_main_cycle.sh` counts `failure | cancelled | timed_out`, producing inconsistent handling of cancelled and startup-failure runs.

- README.md:164 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `PROMOTE_CYCLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` row says that a “job cancelled” counts while the specific note says a cancelled smoke gate is not an attempt.
  WHY: The contradictory operator-facing documentation can cause users to configure the retry budget expecting cancelled runs not to consume it.

- changelog.d/release-gate-retry-budget.md:4 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The changelog states “a cancelled run still never counts” as a blanket rule for both schedulers.
  WHY: This is false for `promote_main_cycle.sh` if cancelled cycle jobs intentionally count, misleading operators about budget consumption; z-ai_glm-5_2 identifies this as the one real defect and disputes the related code findings.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A cancelled smoke gate (`reason=smoke_gate_cancelled`) is a skip, not an attempt."
  expected_change_site: scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh (failed_cycle_heads filter) + tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: Filter at :352 includes cancelled; test asserts it consumes budget; changelog/README mismatch.

- requirement: The changelog lead paragraph ("Both schedulers now count the failed runs on the current tip and dispatch again while the count is below the budget; a cancelled run still never counts") must be consistent with the README and code for the cycle script.
  expected_change_site: `changelog.d/release-gate-retry-budget.md` line 4
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The fragment as filed still asserts the blanket statement; the README `PROMOTE_CYCLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` row and `tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:323-340` (`attempts=3 max=3` from 2 failures + 1 cancelled) document the intentional "cancelled cycle job counts" behavior. Operator-facing text in `CHANGELOG.md` (folded from the fragment at release time) will mislead consumers.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:352 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The jq filter includes .conclusion == "cancelled" when selecting failed cycle runs to count against the retry budget.
  WHY: A cancelled cycle job consumes one of the three retry-budget attempts even though the cycle never proved anything about the tip. Three cancellations hold the tip with no diagnostic. The test at tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:330-340 expects this incorrect behaviour.

- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:352 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The jq filter selects failure|cancelled|timed_out but the parallel auto_release_stable.sh:188 selects failure|timed_out|startup_failure. Neither filter is the correct set: the promote script should count failure|timed_out|startup_failure and exclude cancelled; instead it counts cancelled and excludes startup_failure.
  WHY: A startup_failure cycle-job conclusion would never spend a budget attempt, causing the cycle to dispatch every daily tick against a permanently broken tip. A cancelled cycle-job conclusion prematurely consumes budget that should not count.

- tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:326-340 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test test_failed_runs_on_same_tip_hold_once_the_budget_is_spent encodes the cancelled-as-attempt bug.
  WHY: The test will pass as long as the code includes cancelled in the filter. If the code is fixed to exclude cancelled, this test will need to be updated.

- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:352 (jq filter), 188 (auto_release_stable.sh) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The two schedulers count different conclusion sets against the retry budget.
  WHY: auto_release_stable.sh counts failure|timed_out|startup_failure (no cancelled); promote_main_cycle.sh counts failure|cancelled|timed_out (no startup_failure). The README and changelog say both schedulers follow the same retry-on-transient pattern, but they disagree on what counts.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: A cancelled smoke gate run is documented to be retried on the next tick and to never count against the retry budget, but including it prematurely exhausts the retry budget.

- README.md:164 | severity=NIT | confidence=4

  WHY: This internal contradiction misleads operators.

  PROBLEM: The changelog states "a cancelled run still never counts" as a blanket rule for both schedulers, but `scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh` counts cancelled scheduled cycle runs as attempts.
  WHY: An operator may assume cancelled runs do not consume the budget for `promote_main_cycle.sh`, which is incorrect.
